documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: HPI:
91 yo female with chronic HFpEF, HTN, AF on apixaban, presents with 5 days of progressive dyspnea and leg swelling.
Pt reports orthopnea now requiring 3 pillows, up from 1. Two episodes of PND last night.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Daughter, who lives with pt, reports pt unable to walk to bathroom without stopping to rest.
No chest pain. No fever, cough productive of sputum, or hemoptysis. No recent dietary indiscretion reported, though daughter notes canned soup daily.
Denies syncope, palpitations. No recent med changes other than diuretic increase.
ED course:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED.
PMH:
HFpEF, last echo EF 55-60% with grade 2 diastolic dysfunction
Permanent atrial fibrillation
Hypertension
Osteoarthritis
Hypothyroidism
Remote cholecystectomy
Home medications:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID (recently doubled)
Metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
Apixaban 2.5 mg BID
Levothyroxine 75 mcg daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 650 mg PRN
Social:
Lives with daughter in single-level home. Uses rolling walker at baseline. No tobacco, no alcohol.
Allergies: sulfa - rash
ROS: per HPI, otherwise negative
Physical exam:
Vitals: T 36.7, HR 92 irreg irreg, BP 148/78, RR 26, SpO2 91% on 4L NC
Gen: elderly, frail, speaking in short phrases, sitting upright
HEENT: JVD to angle of jaw at 45 degrees
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, no murmur appreciated, PMI nondisplaced
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally, decreased breath sounds at both bases
Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, warm, pulses palpable
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit
Skin: chronic venous stasis changes both shins, no ulceration
Data:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Na 136, K 3.8, CO2 28, Cl 99, glucose 108
WBC 7.2, Hgb 11.4, Plt 216
Troponin 0.03 flat on repeat
TSH pending
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
ECG: atrial fibrillation at 94, no acute ischemic changes, LVH by voltage
Assessment/Plan:
91 yo female with acute decompensated heart failure, volume overloaded, hypoxemic.
1. Acute CHF exacerbation - furosemide 80 mg IV every 12 hours. Strict I/O, daily standing weight, fluid restrict 1.5 L, 2 g Na diet.
2. Hypoxemia - continue 4L NC, wean as tolerated for SpO2 goal above 90%. Elevate HOB.
3. AF - continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, continue apixaban 2.5 mg BID, rate acceptable.
4. Monitor K with diuresis, replace to keep above 4.0.
5. Cardiology consulted, will see today.
6. Telemetry. DVT ppx per apixaban.
7. Code status: DNR/DNI per prior discussion, reconfirmed with pt and daughter at bedside.
Discussed with daughter at bedside 21:40.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning - Cardiology/Teaching Service
lines: Subjective:
Pt reports breathing somewhat better than admission but still dyspneic turning in bed. Slept on 3 pillows, one episode PND at 02:10.
Voided small amounts overnight per RN. Appetite poor, ate half of breakfast.
Objective:
Vitals: T 36.5, HR 88 irreg, BP 136/72, RR 22, SpO2 91% on 4L NC
Weight 71.2 kg, down 0.6 kg from admission
I/O last 24h: in 640 mL, out 470 mL
Urine output under 500 mL over the past 24 hours despite furosemide 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
Exam: JVD still elevated, crackles to mid fields bilaterally, 3+ edema to thighs unchanged
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, no rub
Alert, oriented, no distress at rest
Labs: Na 135, K 3.6, CO2 29, Hgb 11.2
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute CHF exacerbation, inadequate diuretic response. Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL. Stop intermittent dosing.
2. Foley deferred; use urinal/bedside commode with strict measurement. Recheck I/O at 6 hour intervals.
3. Hypoxemia - remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2. Continue, attempt wean this afternoon if crackles improve.
4. K 3.6 - KCl 40 mEq PO now, repeat BMP this afternoon.
5. Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily and apixaban 2.5 mg BID.
6. Daily weights, fluid restrict 1.5 L, 2 g Na diet continue.
7. PT eval for mobility once diuresis established.
Cardiology in agreement with infusion plan, discussed at 09:15.
Plan reviewed with pt and daughter.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon - Interval Update
lines: Subjective:
Interval re-eval at 16:30. Pt reports easier breathing, able to speak full sentences. No chest pain.
Passed urine three times since 11:00, larger volumes per RN.
Objective:
Vitals at 16:00: HR 84 irreg, BP 128/70, RR 18, SpO2 93% on 4L NC
Urine output since 10:30 start of infusion: 820 mL over 6 hours
Exam: crackles now at bases only, JVD to clavicle at 45 degrees, edema 2+ to knees
No orthostatic symptoms with bedside sitting
Repeat BMP: Na 136, K 4.1, CO2 30
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute CHF exacerbation - good response to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr. Continue overnight, reassess for conversion to PO in AM.
2. Volume - net negative today. Continue strict I/O, standing weight in AM.
3. Oxygen - SpO2 improving; attempted wean to 2L NC at 17:00, will recheck sat in 30 min and with ambulation.
4. K repleted and adequate at 4.1, recheck in AM with diuresis ongoing.
5. BP stable, no hypotension on infusion. Hold no meds.
6. Continue apixaban 2.5 mg BID, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
7. PT saw pt at 15:00, ambulated 20 feet with rolling walker, tolerated.
8. Anticipate transition to PO diuretic and discharge planning with daughter tomorrow if trajectory holds.
RN updated on wean plan and I/O documentation.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - CHF Exacerbation - Discharged HD3
lines: Discharge diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure (HFpEF), hypoxemia, permanent atrial fibrillation, hypokalemia (resolved)
Length of stay: 3 days, discharged HD3
Hospital course:
91 yo female with HFpEF and permanent AF admitted with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea and leg edema.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Response to infusion was brisk with 820 mL out over the first 6 hours. Infusion continued overnight and stopped 08:00 HD3.
Transitioned to PO diuretic HD3 morning. Net negative 2.9 L for the admission; discharge weight 68.9 kg.
Oxygen weaned from 4L to 2L NC on HD2 evening and to room air HD3 at 09:40 with SpO2 93% at rest and 91% after ambulating 100 feet with walker.
K 3.6 on HD2 repleted with KCl 40 mEq PO, 4.1 on recheck, 4.0 at discharge.
Troponin flat, ECG showed AF without ischemic change. No indication for ischemic workup this admission.
Cardiology followed throughout and agreed with discharge regimen.
Discharge exam: HR 80 irreg, BP 126/74, RR 18, SpO2 93% RA, crackles cleared, JVD not elevated, 1+ ankle edema.
Discharge medications:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID
Potassium chloride 20 mEq PO daily
Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily
Apixaban 2.5 mg PO BID
Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain
Instructions:
Weigh daily each morning after voiding, same scale, record. Call for gain of 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in 3 days.
Fluid restriction 1.5 L daily. Sodium under 2 g daily; avoid canned soups and processed meats.
Return or call for worsening shortness of breath, inability to lie flat, new leg swelling, chest pain, or lightheadedness.
Follow-up:
Cardiology clinic in 5 to 7 days for volume and electrolyte recheck.
Primary care in 2 weeks.
Home health RN for weight and med review, arranged prior to discharge.
Condition at discharge: stable, ambulating with rolling walker, on room air.
Discharged to home with daughter at 13:20. Instructions reviewed with pt and daughter; teach-back completed.
Code status: DNR/DNI, unchanged.
